checks: Source 39a2ef7b63aae46b §2 gives the strict and attained weak variants, the median and trimmed applications, and the compact two-atom sharpness example.

At an intermediate point monotonicity supplies the left ray for the first law and the right ray for the second. If neither law already works, affinity along their mixture reaches left-ray mass exactly t. Closed rays cover the line, so its right mass is at least 1−t, which suffices through t=1/2 even if the rays overlap at an atom.
For a strict superlevel below 1/2 a common intermediate threshold exists and a witness at each endpoint follows from the supremum. Weak membership uses attainment exactly as claimed.

The compact median domain is a finite union of clopen base strata. The continuous target map has closed ray pullbacks, and the smaller cap mass is upper semicontinuous by Portmanteau. The central-central block is clopen and its probability is continuous, so a nonempty trimmed set remains weakly compact and convex. The same fixed-point reasoning also works outside the fiber.
The compact convex two-atom family has value 1 at the atoms and 1/2 at interior points by maximizing min(θ,1−θ), so every weak level strictly above 1/2 up to 1 gives a failure.

dependencies.hypotheses: Its compact median pair domain and segment map apply with d=1. The frozen proof uses its continuity and weak compactness, then separately treats closed-ray payoffs and the central-central restriction.

overlap.comparison: This provides the compact coupling domain and continuous map. It proves attainment of target depth, without the interval-shape assertion for either convex law families or trimmed couplings.
Its convex regions concern one ordinary uniform volume law and are not a supremum over different laws.
